title: Rajasuya and the First Honour
body:
Rajasuya and the First Honour

पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति ।
तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ।।

"If one offers to Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or even water, I delightfully partake of that article offered with love by My devotee in pure consciousness. (Gita IX-26)"

With Jarasandha slain and the imprisoned kings liberated, Yudhishthira's Rajasuya Yajna proceeded in unparalleled majesty. This grand sacrifice attracted sages, preceptors, and monarchs from across Bharatavarsha. The ritual climaxed at the ceremony of offering the Arghya—the first and highest honor of the assembly—to the most worthy individual present. Under Bheeshma's authoritative recommendation, Sahadeva presented the first honor to Lord Shree Krishna, acknowledging Him as the supreme refuge of all living beings.
This choice incensed Shishupala, the King of Chedi. Driven by a long-standing personal envy and blinded by material egotism, Shishupala launched into a venomous tirade, mocking Bheeshma as a senile dotard and Yudhishthira as an ignorant youth. He derided Shree Krishna as a 'cowherd boor' of no royal blood, unworthy of precedence over venerable teachers like Drona or sages like Vyasa. Shishupala's speech represented the absolute limits of spiritual blindness, treating the Supreme Lord as a mere mortal bound by social hierarchies.
Shree Krishna sat in serene silence, patiently counting Shishupala's insults until they reached one hundred, fulfilling a promise of forbearance He had made to Shishupala's mother. When the hundred and first insult escaped Shishupala's lips, Shree Krishna released His Sudarshana Chakra, decapitating the Chedi king in the middle of the assembly. A brilliant light then emerged from Shishupala's fallen body and merged into the feet of the Lord, demonstrating that even those who oppose the Divine out of intense concentration (albeit through hatred) are ultimately absorbed back into the Supreme Source.
